title: Finite rectangular quotients with arbitrarily small metric oscillation
statement:
Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen (open and closed) subsets, and let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group whose identity has a neighbourhood basis of open normal subgroups. Let $r\geq1$ be an integer, $(Y,d_Y)$ any metric space, $f:S\times G^r\to Y$ continuous, and $\epsilon>0$. There exist a finite clopen partition $\mathcal P$ of $S$ and an open normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq G$ such that, for any $s,s'\in S$ in the same part and $g_i,g_i'\in G$ with $g_iN=g_i'N$ for $1\leq i\leq r$,
$$d_Y\bigl(f(s,g_1,\ldots,g_r),f(s',g_1',\ldots,g_r')\bigr)<\epsilon.$$
Here a finite clopen partition is a finite set of pairwise disjoint nonempty clopen subsets with union $S$; for empty $S$ it is the empty partition. If $A=\mathcal P$ and $B=G/N$, both with their discrete topologies, then $B$ is a finite group, the part map $p:S\to A$ and quotient homomorphism $q:G\to B$ are continuous surjections, and the displayed bound holds on every fibre of $p\times q^r$. No completeness of $Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: If $S=\varnothing$, take $\mathcal P=\varnothing$ and $N=G$. The bound is vacuous, $A=\varnothing$, and $B=G/G$ is the one-element discrete group. The unique map $S\to A$ and the constant quotient map $G\to B$ are continuous surjections. Hence suppose $S\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image coefficient comparison: agent-written auxiliary topological argument; the current blueprint does not state or prove this auxiliary assertion.

proof.text: For $x=(s,g_1,\ldots,g_r)\in S\times G^r$, continuity makes $O_x=f^{-1}(B_Y(f(x),\epsilon/2))$ an open neighbourhood of $x$. By the finite-product topology choose open neighbourhoods $U_x$ of $s$ and $V_{x,i}$ of $g_i$ with $U_x\times\prod_iV_{x,i}\subseteq O_x$. The assumed clopen basis gives a clopen $C_x$ with $s\in C_x\subseteq U_x$. The set $\{h:g_i h\in V_{x,i}\}$ is an open neighbourhood of $1$, since multiplication by the fixed $g_i$ is continuous. By the assumed identity basis choose an open normal subgroup $H_{x,i}$ inside it. Then $R_x=C_x\times\prod_i g_iH_{x,i}$ contains $x$ and lies in $O_x$. Each coset $g_iH_{x,i}$ is open: it is the inverse image of $H_{x,i}$ under the continuous map $t\mapsto g_i^{-1}t$. Thus the $R_x$ form an open cover, and $d_Y(f(y),f(x))<\epsilon/2$ for $y\in R_x$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] to the finite family consisting of $S$ and $r$ copies of $G$. Its product is $S\times G^r$ with exactly the topology used above, so it is compact. The definition of compactness gives a finite subcover $R_{x_1},\ldots,R_{x_m}$. Write $x_j=(s_j,g_{j,1},\ldots,g_{j,r})$, $C_j=C_{x_j}$, and $H_{j,i}=H_{x_j,i}$. Since $S\ne\varnothing$ and $1\in G$, the product is nonempty and $m\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 08ZU, theorem-tychonov: a product of quasi-compact spaces is quasi-compact; finite open-subcover definition.

proof.text: For each membership pattern $e:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,1\}$ form $P_e=\bigcap_{j=1}^m D_{j,e(j)}$, where $D_{j,1}=C_j$ and $D_{j,0}=S\setminus C_j$. Discard the empty $P_e$ and let $\mathcal P$ be the resulting finite set. Finite intersections of clopens are clopen. Every point has exactly one membership pattern, and distinct patterns give disjoint sets. Thus $\mathcal P$ is a finite clopen partition of $S$, and every part meeting $C_j$ is contained in $C_j$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image coefficient comparison: agent-written auxiliary topological argument; the current blueprint does not state or prove this auxiliary assertion.

proof.text: Set $N=\bigcap_{1\leq j\leq m,\,1\leq i\leq r}H_{j,i}$. This is an open normal subgroup: it is a subgroup by closure of each $H_{j,i}$ under products and inverses, it is normal because conjugation preserves every $H_{j,i}$, and it is open as a finite intersection of opens. In particular $N\subseteq H_{j,i}$ for every $j,i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image coefficient comparison: agent-written auxiliary topological argument; the current blueprint does not state or prove this auxiliary assertion.

proof.text: Let $y=(s,h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ and $y'=(s',h_1',\ldots,h_r')$ satisfy the hypotheses of the displayed bound. Choose $j$ with $y\in R_{x_j}$. The common partition part of $s,s'$ meets $C_j$, so $s'\in C_j$. Since $h_iN=h_i'N$, write $h_i'=h_i n_i$ with $n_i\in N$. Writing $h_i=g_{j,i}a_i$ with $a_i\in H_{j,i}$ gives $h_i'=g_{j,i}(a_i n_i)\in g_{j,i}H_{j,i}$. Hence both points lie in $R_{x_j}$, and the triangle inequality gives $d_Y(f(y),f(y'))\leq d_Y(f(y),f(x_j))+d_Y(f(x_j),f(y'))<\epsilon/2+\epsilon/2=\epsilon$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image coefficient comparison: agent-written auxiliary topological argument; the current blueprint does not state or prove this auxiliary assertion.

proof.text: Give $A=\mathcal P$ the discrete topology and let $p(s)$ be its unique containing part. Every part is nonempty, so $p$ is surjective; the inverse image of any subset of $A$ is a union of open parts, so $p$ is continuous. Normality of $N$ makes multiplication $(gN)(hN)=(gh)N$ and inversion $(gN)^{-1}=g^{-1}N$ well-defined, giving the quotient group $B=G/N$ and the surjective homomorphism $q(g)=gN$. Its cosets are open by the same fixed-translation inverse-image argument as above. They cover compact $G$, so finitely many cover $G$; distinct cosets are disjoint, hence these are all cosets and $B$ is finite. For the discrete topology on $B$, every subset has open inverse image, a union of cosets; thus $q$ is continuous. Equality of images under $p\times q^r$ is exactly the hypothesis used in the previous step. This proves the fibre bound, and no step used completeness of $Y$.
